introduction.heading: 1. Introduction
introduction.text: At TempEmail, we take your privacy seriously. This Privacy Policy explains how we handle information when you use our temporary email service. Our core principle is simple: we collect minimal data and prioritize your anonymity.

dont_collect.heading: 2. Information We Don't Collect
dont_collect.text: We are committed to not collecting personal information. Specifically, we do not collect:

items.name_email: Your name, email address, or contact information
items.persistent_ids: Persistent identifiers that track you across sessions
items.browsing_history: Your browsing history outside our service

temp_process.heading: 3. Information We Temporarily Process
temp_process.text: To provide our service, we temporarily process:

items.received_emails: Emails received at those temporary addresses
items.technical_data: Technical data necessary for email delivery (sender, timestamp, subject)
items.analytics: Basic analytics to maintain service performance (anonymous usage statistics)

temp_process.note: All this data is automatically deleted when your temporary email expires or is manually deleted by you.

data_retention.heading: 4. Data Retention
data_retention.text: Temporary email addresses and their contents are stored only for the duration of the session or the extended time period you select. Once expired, all data is permanently deleted from our servers. We do not maintain backups of expired email content.

cookies_tracking.heading: 5. Cookies and Tracking
cookies_tracking.text: We use minimal cookies solely for service functionality (such as maintaining your temporary email session). We do not use tracking cookies or third-party advertising cookies. You can use our service without accepting cookies, though some features may be limited.

third_party.heading: 6. Third-Party Services
third_party.text: We do not share your data with third parties for marketing or advertising purposes. We may use essential third-party services for infrastructure (such as hosting providers), but these services are contractually bound to protect your data and not use it for their own purposes.

security.heading: 7. Security
security.text: We implement industry-standard security measures to protect the temporary data we process. This includes encryption in transit (HTTPS), secure server configurations, and regular security audits. However, no method of transmission over the internet is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

content_warnings.heading: 8. Content Warnings
content_warnings.text: Our content safety feature analyzes incoming emails for potentially harmful content (phishing attempts, malware links, explicit content). This analysis is performed automatically and does not involve human review of your emails.

your_rights.heading: 9. Your Rights
your_rights.text: You have the right to delete your temporary email and all associated data at any time by simply closing or clearing your session. Since we don't collect personal information, there is no personal data to request, modify, or delete beyond the temporary email content itself.

child_privacy.heading: 10. Children's Privacy
child_privacy.text: Our service is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect information from children. If you believe a child has used our service, please contact us.

international_users.heading: 11. International Users
international_users.text: TempEmail is accessible globally. By using our service, you consent to the processing of data in the country where our servers are located. We comply with applicable data protection laws and regulations.

changes_policy.heading: 12. Changes to This Policy
changes_policy.text: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify users of significant changes by posting a notice on our service. Continued use after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

contact_us.heading: 13. Contact Us
contact_us.text: If you have questions or concerns about this Privacy Policy or our privacy practices, please contact us through our support channels. We are committed to addressing your concerns promptly.

whatIs.title: What Is Temp Mail for OTP?
whatIs.boldOpener: A temporary email for OTP is a disposable, anonymous inbox
whatIs.p1: used to receive one-time passwords from websites, apps, and online services — without handing over your real email address.
whatIs.p2: When a service needs to verify your identity, it sends a short-lived code to your email. That code is the OTP. Normally you'd provide your permanent inbox, creating a permanent link between your identity and that service. With a temp mail, you give a throwaway address instead. The OTP arrives all the same, you enter it, and the address disappears afterward.
whatIs.p3: No registration, no commitment, no residue. Temporary email services generate a fresh, fully functional inbox in seconds — and when you're done, so is the address.

howItWorks.title: How It Works
howItWorks.intro: Using a disposable email for OTP verification takes under a minute. Here's the full process:
howItWorks.outro: The entire flow leaves no digital footprint. Once the inbox expires, there is no record that it ever existed.

steps.0: Open TempEmail — a disposable inbox is generated automatically. No sign-up, no captcha, no personal information required.
steps.1: Copy the address with one click, or scan the QR code to send it directly to your phone.
steps.2: Paste the address into the signup form or verification field of whichever service is requesting your OTP.
steps.3: The one-time password arrives in real time. Copy it, complete the verification, and walk away — the inbox auto-expires and all messages are permanently deleted.

callouts.qrText: Started on desktop but need to verify on your phone? Scan the built-in QR code to send your temp mail address directly to your mobile device — same inbox, no typing, no errors.

benefits.title: Benefits of Using Temp Mail for OTP
benefits.intro: A disposable email address does one thing better than any other tool: it separates your real identity from the services asking for it. Here's why that matters for OTP verification specifically.
benefits.privacyText: Every service you hand your real email to knows who you are. Over time, that list grows — and so does the exposure. A temporary email breaks that chain entirely. The service gets a valid address for OTP delivery and nothing else. Your actual inbox, your name, and your online history remain untouched.
benefits.spamText: Services that require OTP verification often treat your email address as a marketing asset afterward. A disposable inbox cuts off that pipeline at the source. When the inbox expires, the mailing list entry expires with it.
benefits.accessText: Unlike every other email provider, temp mail requires nothing from you. No username, no password, no recovery phone number. The inbox is live the moment you open the page — which is exactly what you need when you're mid-signup on another service and just need a code.
benefits.speedText: Temporary inboxes receive email at the same speed as any permanent address. OTPs typically arrive within seconds of being sent. The inbox refreshes live, so there's no need to reload while waiting for a time-sensitive code.

benefitItems.0: No account or personal data required to create an inbox
benefitItems.1: Inbox expires automatically, deleting all messages permanently
benefitItems.2: Compatible with virtually any service that supports email-based OTP
benefitItems.3: Time extension keeps your inbox alive if verification takes longer than expected
benefitItems.4: Safe content warnings flag suspicious emails before you open them

useCases.title: When to Use a Disposable Email for OTP
useCases.intro: Any time a service wants your email for a one-time or low-commitment interaction, a temporary address is the right call. Here are the most common situations.
useCases.onlineText: Many sites gate content, downloads, or features behind a verified account. If you only need access once — or you're not sure you'll return — there's no reason to commit your real address.
useCases.appText: Mobile apps and web platforms increasingly require OTP verification before granting access. A temp mail handles that step without tying your permanent email to the account.
useCases.otpText: One-time passwords are used for account activation, password resets, and guest access. In all of these cases the email only needs to receive a single message — making a disposable inbox a natural fit.

useCaseOnline.0: Free trial accounts for software or SaaS tools you're evaluating
useCaseOnline.1: Forums and communities requiring email confirmation to post
useCaseOnline.2: News or content sites gating articles behind a registered account
useCaseOnline.3: E-commerce platforms requiring registration before you can browse

useCaseApp.0: Secondary or test accounts on social media platforms
useCaseApp.1: Gaming services and launchers that use email-based login
useCaseApp.2: Streaming or media platforms with email-verified free tiers
useCaseApp.3: Beta programs and early access invites requiring sign-in

useCaseOtp.0: Account activation codes sent immediately after registration
useCaseOtp.1: Email-based two-factor authentication for temporary sessions
useCaseOtp.2: Password reset links for services you no longer actively use
useCaseOtp.3: One-time login codes for guest checkouts or limited access portals

safety.title: Safety Tips
safety.intro: Temp mail is a practical privacy tool, but it works best when you understand what it is and isn't suited for.
safety.warn1Text: TempEmail scans incoming messages for suspicious content. If an email contains potentially harmful links, scripts, or attachments, a warning is shown before you open the message. This protects you from phishing attempts that may arrive through the OTP process.
safety.warn2Text: Every inbox has a built-in countdown. Once it runs out, all messages are permanently deleted with no recovery option. If you need more time, use the time extension feature before the timer hits zero.
safety.warn3Text: Never use a disposable address for accounts you intend to keep — banking, primary social media, or anything where losing access to the email means losing access to the account permanently. Temp mail is for throwaway or one-time interactions only.
safety.warn4Text: Messages are not stored after inbox expiration. If you need to reference something from an OTP email later — a confirmation number, a link, a reference code — save it before the inbox expires.
safety.outro: Within those boundaries, disposable email is one of the lowest-effort, highest-impact privacy tools available for everyday online activity.

0.q: Is it safe to use temp mail for OTP verification?
0.a: Yes, for the vast majority of OTP use cases it is completely safe. Temporary inboxes receive email identically to any permanent address. TempEmail also adds safe content warnings on flagged messages. The main risk is inbox expiration — avoid using temp mail for accounts where you'll need long-term access.

1.q: How long does a temporary email inbox last?
1.a: By default, inboxes stay active for 10 minutes after the last activity. The time extension feature lets you keep the inbox alive longer without losing existing messages. Once the timer runs out, all emails are permanently and irrecoverably deleted.

2.q: Will every service accept a temporary email address?
2.a: Most services accept any syntactically valid email, including disposable ones. Some larger platforms maintain blocklists of known temp mail domains. TempEmail rotates across multiple domains to maximize compatibility with services that filter disposable addresses.

3.q: Can I use temp mail for two-factor authentication?
3.a: For email-based 2FA, yes — the temporary inbox receives authentication codes just like a permanent address. However, if you're setting up long-term 2FA on an account you plan to keep, use your real email or an authenticator app. Losing the temp inbox means losing access to that 2FA method.

4.q: Does TempEmail store my messages or track my usage?
4.a: No personal information is required to use TempEmail, and all messages are permanently deleted when the inbox expires. No email address, name, or persistent identifier is collected or retained after a session ends.
